items.description:
Announcing the general availability of resumable uploads for
Azure Storage Blob SFTP. In the event of a failed partial transfer, this new
feature enables users to open the partial file and continue writing the
remaining content. This capability optimizes time and conserves network
bandwidth, especially in situations where network interruptions occur during
file transfers, such as in remote areas with low connectivity or when
transferring large files like multimedia or seismic data etc.  Resume Upload  The resumable upload feature for Azure Blob Storage SFTP is
now generally available. This feature allows users to resume file uploads from
the point of failure in the event of partial transfer failures, thereby saving
time and reducing network bandwidth usage.  Learn
more. The SFTP transfer modes that Azure Blob Storage SFTP
supports are below: Write: This mode lets the
client continue an upload by adding data to an existing file from a specific
point without creating a new file.  Write + Create: This mode
allows the client to resume an upload by either adding to an existing file or
creating a new one if it doesn't exist, providing flexibility when the file may
not be present initially.  Append: This mode adds data
to the end of an existing file without overwriting its current contents.  Resumable upload enhances efficiency by saving time and
bandwidth during interrupted file transfers. Please reach out to
blobsftp@microsoft.com for feedback about SFTP for Azure Blob Storage.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Blob Storage SFTP - Resumable Uploads

items.description: On June 30, 2026, AzureML SDK V1 will reach end of life. The following SDKs which work in tandem with the AzureML SDK V1 will also be retired.  azureml-train-core  azureml-pipeline  azureml-pipeline-core  azureml-pipeline-internal  azureml-pipeline-steps  After June 30, 2026, you can continue to use these SDKs, however they will not be supported and may stop working without notice.  Recommended action  To ensure that you are using a supported SDK for your workloads, it is recommended to migrate to AzureML SDK V1 before 30 Jun 2026.  Detailed guidance is documented here.Help and support  If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support case.  Links provided herein may take you to a third-party website and are provided for convenience only. Third-party websites are subject to the third-party's terms and privacy statements.  Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.
items.title: Retirement: Remove dependency on these Azure ML SDKs before June 30, 2026

items.description: In 2026, Azure Resource Manager will be deprecating the Custom Resource Provider (CuRP) service.We will retire the feature by October 31, 2026. We will be performing a scream test on October 27, 2025, as part of this deprecation. On July 31, 2026, creates, updates, patches, and actions to custom resources and resource providers will be blocked. You will only be able to read and delete your custom resources and resource providers.We understand that this deprecation may be an inconvenience to you and your team. Here are some potential CuRP alternatives you can use to support your existing workflows.If your CuRP scenario:Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, consider Deployment Scripts.Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, and you use Bicep, consider Bicep Extensions.Involves triggering several different endpoints or services for your solution, consider Azure Functions.If you have any questions, please ask your Microsoft account manager to email curpdeprecation@microsoft.com with your name, company name, email contact, and subscription ID.
items.title: Retirement: Deprecation of Custom Resource Providers

items.description: The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026. This change aligns with the broader Azure Virtual Network (VNet) update and replaces the previously communicated September 30, 2025 date. Starting March 31, 2026, newly created VNets will default to using private subnets. This means: Explicit outbound connectivity (e.g., via NAT Gateway, UDR, or other methods) must be configured to access public endpoints on the Internet or Microsoft services. Default outbound access will be disabled by default, but not removed. Customers who do not configure an outbound method will lose internet connectivity from their Batch nodes. Review your current Batch pool configurations, especially those using simplified node communication without public IPs.Plan to implement an explicit outbound method before the March 2026 deadline. Learn more:Read Default Internet outbound access for Simplified node communication Batch pools without public IP addresses will be retired on 30 September 2025.Read How and when default outbound access is providedRead Feature Update: Default behavior for newly created virtual networks will be private
items.title: Update: The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026.

items.description:
The Azure MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server provides a
streamlined approach for managing Azure resources—including Azure confidential ledger—through
natural language prompts. This feature allows users to interact with confidential
ledger without the need to memorize complex command syntax. Customers can now
create an immutable and integrity-protected Azure confidential ledger for
logging purposes. Additionally, writing to and reading from the ledger using AI
is now fully supported and ready for deployment.You can connect to Azure MCP Server
utilizing a range of tools, programming languages, and frameworks. The server
facilitates resource management via natural language conversations, supports
the development of automation scripts, and enables integration of Azure
operations into various applications. This capability is accessible through
Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Availaible: Azure MCP Server support for Azure confidential ledger

items.description:
We are announcing the general availability of the Perth
Azure Extended Zone.   Azure Extended Zones are small-footprint extensions of Azure
placed in metro areas, industry centers, or specific jurisdictions, to serve
low latency and data residency workloads. They support a selection of virtual
machine (VMs), container, networking, storage, and other Azure services. Azure
Extended Zones can run latency-sensitive and throughput-intensive applications
close to end users, within data residency boundaries.  Learn more
about onboarding and managing Azure Extended Zones on our learn page, and start
unlocking low-latency performance for your Perth workloads.
items.title: Generally Available: Perth - Azure Extended Zones

items.description: Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection (ANF ARP) is now in Public Preview.  ANF ARP is designed to help organizations proactively detect, respond to, and recover from ransomware threats on cloud volumes. ANF ARP monitors Azure NetApp Files volumes for suspicious activity using file extension profiling, entropy, and IOPS patterns. When a threat is detected, the system creates a point-in-time snapshot, enabling rapid evaluation and recovery. Notifications are sent via Azure Activity log and attack reports are retained for 30 days. There is no specific additional charge for ANF ARP but see Considerations section when sizing your deployment to accommodate ANF ARP. Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection is now Public Preview in all regions.Learn more:  What's new in Azure NetApp Files  Configure Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection
items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection

items.description:
The Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2
is a US government standard that defines minimum security requirements for
cryptographic modules in information technology products and systems. Azure Application Gateway V2 now supports FIPS mode,
which can be enabled during deployment or at any time afterward. When FIPS mode
is turned on, the gateway uses only FIPS-compliant predefined and custom TLS
policies, enhancing security and helping meet FedRAMP security requirements. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: FIPS compliant mode for Application Gateway V2 SKUs

items.description: Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks are now available in Public Preview, offering a fully managed workspace type that comes preconfigured with serverless compute and default storage to deliver an enterprise-ready SaaS experience with minimal infrastructure setup. With this release, customers can create Azure Databricks “Serverless” workspaces directly from the Azure portal to run production workloads entirely on serverless compute, rapidly spin up short-lived environments for training and testing, and empower admins who lack direct cloud provisioning permissions to deploy and manage secure, governed Azure Databricks environments at scale. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Serverless workspaces in Azure Databricks

items.description:
Bandwidth metrics for Azure Load
Balancer are now published with metric dimension Protocol. When retrieving or
viewing Byte, Packet, and SYN Count metrics in the Azure portal, you will now
see the dimension Protocol. TCP traffic is denoted by Protocol=6, while UDP
traffic is represented by Protocol=17. With the Protocol dimension, you
gain more granular visibility into traffic patterns for alerting, monitoring,
and troubleshooting requirements. The Protocol dimension is
available on Byte, Packet, and SYN Count metrics in all Azure public regions,
China cloud regions, and Government cloud regions. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Load Balancer bandwidth metrics now support Protocol dimension

items.description: Cross-zone-region replication builds on the existing capabilities of cross-region replication and cross-zone replication. It enables you to replicate volumes across regions and across availability zones within the same region, combining disaster recovery and business continuance capabilities for volumes. To establish two protection volumes, you create a cross-zone replication relationship, and a cross-region replication relationship, two cross-region replication relationships or two cross-zone replication relationships. The source volume should be in an availability zone for the cross-zone replication relationship.  This feature is now GA and available in these Regions  Learn more: What's new in Azure NetApp Files   Azure Availability Zones Create a CZRR for Azure NetApp Files
items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files cross-zone-region replication (CZRR)

items.description: Zonal Placement for Azure Files Premium LRS is now GA in select regions! This capability gives you explicit control over zone locality by pinning storage accounts to a specific availability zone, enabling high availability, fault isolation, and predictable low-latency performance for mission-critical workloads. Why it matters: Align compute and storage in the same zone for 10–40% lower latency compared to cross-zone deployments. Design resilient architectures with zone-aware control for better fault isolation.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Zonal placement for Azure file shares Azure Files Premium LRS in select regions.

items.description: Azure Sphere OS version 25.12 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. Whilst this release encompasses no customer-facing changes, it represents significant under-the-hood build system changes, as such, this release will operate for an extended evaluation period, until February 2026, enabling additional time for customer evaluation testing.Following this period, a second evaluation release, 26.02, will be launched to the Retail Eval feed for the standard 14-day testing period, and subsequently promoted to the Retail feed. This means that 25.12 will not be promoted to the Retail feed, and that the next Retail release will be 26.02.During this time, please verify that your applications and devices operate properly with both the 25.12, and subsequent 26.02 release, before it is deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed. The 25.12 OS Retail Eval release includes significant underlying build system updates.Learn more:For more information on Azure Sphere OS feeds and setting up an evaluation device group, see Azure Sphere OS feeds and Set up devices for OS evaluation.For self-help inquiries or technical support, review the Azure Sphere support options.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 25.12 is now available for evaluation

items.description: You can now simplify how you diagnose and resolve issues in your applications running on Azure Cosmos DB with the introduction of the Azure Cosmos DB Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Agent, built on the Azure SRE Agent platform. This new capability gives you deeper visibility into the health and performance of your database workloads by combining client-side telemetry with server-side diagnostics, allowing you to identify problems faster and understand them more clearly.  Using the Azure Cosmos DB SRE Agent, you receive recommendations that help you improve performance, strengthen security, and optimize cost. Instead of only detecting issues, the agent guides you through best practices tailored to your workload. You can use it to understand why throttling may be occurring, how configuration choices impact performance or reliability, or whether your application is encountering hidden connectivity challenges. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Use Azure SRE Agent with Azure Cosmos DB

items.description:
Azure Storage Mover’s new Azure Blob container-to-container
migration feature is now in Public Preview, empowering organizations to move
data between two Blob containers within the same or different storage accounts, subscriptions or Azure regions securely, reliably, and at scale. With this release, customers can
eliminate manual pipelines and tools, automate migrations in the Azure portal,
and gain real-time visibility into every job. Key benefits: 1. Fully Managed and Scalable Azure Storage Mover is a fully managed service, meaning
Microsoft handles the infrastructure, scaling, and reliability. This reduces
operational overhead and ensures consistent performance across large-scale
transfers. 2. No Agent Required Unlike on-premises migrations, cloud-to-cloud transfers do
not require deploying an agent. This simplifies setup and reduces the need for
additional compute resources. 3. High-Speed, Parallel Transfers Storage Mover supports parallel file transfers, enabling
faster migration of large datasets. This is particularly useful when moving
data across regions or between storage accounts with high throughput
requirements. Get started today and simplify your cloud data estate with
Azure Storage Mover’s Blob-to-Blob migration. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Blob-to-Blob migration made simple with Azure Storage Mover
